summary: Republican Sen. Tom Cotton leads Democratic farmer Hallie Shoffner 50 to 41 in an October Talk Business and Hendrix College poll, after an August poll from the same pollster had Shoffner narrowly ahead, per Political Wire and Talk Business. Shoffner is running on the farm crisis, tariffs and fuel prices tied to the Iran war, while Cotton, who has vastly outspent her, has focused on her past comments about defunding ICE and her Democratic donations, per Newsweek and Fox News.

issues.issue: Farm crisis and the farm bill
issues.why: Arkansas leads the nation in farm bankruptcies and Congress has not passed a full farm bill since 2018.
Shoffner blames Trump's trade wars and the Iran war for higher prices at the pump that squeeze farmers and families.
Cotton's ads feature Shoffner saying she would defund ICE as it exists, and she now says she wants to reform the agency.
Shoffner targets monopolies in seed, fertilizer and meatpacking that she says squeeze Arkansas growers.
Shoffner raised concerns about data centers driving up power use and utility bills.

storylines.title: October poll shows Cotton up nine
storylines.what: A Talk Business and Hendrix College poll had Cotton at 50 percent, Shoffner at 41 and Libertarian Jeff Wadlin at 5.

storylines.title: No Cotton Shoffner debate
storylines.what: Salem Media withdrew its offer to host the only debate Cotton accepted, and Shoffner said Cotton is either too good or too scared to face her.

storylines.title: Cotton skips Arkansas TV debate
storylines.what: Shoffner and Wadlin debated in Conway without Cotton, with Shoffner tying him to the Iran war and votes against past farm bills.

storylines.title: Shoffner ad features former Cotton voter
storylines.what: A Shoffner ad features a former Cotton voter criticizing him for voting down the farm bill twice.

storylines.title: Cotton outspending Shoffner 65 to 1
storylines.what: Cotton and allies had spent about 13.6 million dollars on ads to roughly 209,000 for Shoffner, with no national Democratic money in the race.

storylines.title: Shoffner shifts on ICE
storylines.what: After Cotton ads used her June pledge to defund ICE, Shoffner wrote that she does not want to defund ICE but reform it.

storylines.title: August poll shows Shoffner ahead
storylines.what: A Talk Business and Hendrix poll had Shoffner at 47 percent and Cotton at 44, within the margin of error.

events.title: Defund ICE clip
events.prompt: Attack ads are replaying a recorded pledge to defund ICE as it exists today, and early voting has begun. How do you handle immigration enforcement?

opts.label: Stand by defunding
opts.say: Say ICE as it exists is abusive and should not get another dime.

opts.label: Reform, not defund
opts.say: Back deporting violent criminals while requiring visible badges and no masks for agents.

opts.label: Fund full enforcement
opts.say: Promise more money for ICE and back the president's deportation push.

events.title: Farm bill and tariffs
events.prompt: Arkansas leads the nation in farm bankruptcies, there is no new farm bill, and tariffs and fuel prices are squeezing growers. What is your answer?

opts.label: End blanket tariffs
opts.say: Oppose blanket tariffs, pass a farm bill and break up agriculture monopolies.

opts.label: Targeted aid and tariffs
opts.say: Back targeted tariffs and bridge payments to farmers until markets recover.

opts.label: Back the trade fight
opts.say: Defend the president's tariffs as leverage that will open markets for Arkansas crops.

events.title: Debate invitations
events.prompt: Your only agreed debate host withdrew and a public TV station is holding a debate with the third party candidate. Do you show up?

opts.label: Debate anywhere
opts.say: Accept every invitation and call out anyone who refuses.

opts.label: One head to head
opts.say: Offer new dates for a single two way debate on a friendly outlet.

opts.label: Skip debates
opts.say: Skip debates and campaign at local events, relying on paid ads.

events.title: Iran war and gas prices
events.prompt: Fuel prices have spiked since the Iran war began in February, and your opponent says the war is driving up costs. How do you respond?

opts.label: Blame the war hawks
opts.say: Say the war was a mistake pushed for years and Arkansans pay at the pump.

opts.label: Focus on relief
opts.say: Avoid the war debate and push relief for fuel and fertilizer costs.

opts.label: Defend strength abroad
opts.say: Argue that confronting Iran keeps America safe and prices will ease.

ads.theme: Uses Shoffner's own recorded remarks, including a pledge to defund ICE, to argue she is extreme.

ads.by: America One and Arkansans for Democracy and Justice
ads.theme: Pro Cotton super PACs spent over 3 million dollars on ads and texts.
A former Cotton voter says Cotton voted down the farm bill twice.

regions.name: Central Arkansas
regions.note: Little Rock in Pulaski is the Democratic anchor, ringed by fast growing Republican suburbs.

regions.name: Northwest Arkansas
regions.note: A booming, more diverse region where Fayetteville leans left and Benton County is Republican but trending less so.

regions.name: The Delta
regions.note: Heavily agricultural and majority Black in places, the Democratic base outside Little Rock and the heart of the farm crisis.

regions.name: Northeast Arkansas
regions.note: Rice and soybean country around Jonesboro, near Shoffner's home, that has become solidly Republican.

regions.name: Ozarks and the north
regions.note: Rural, older and deeply Republican mountain counties.

regions.name: South Arkansas
regions.note: Timber and oil towns plus Hot Springs, mostly Republican with Democratic pockets in Black communities.
